date: 13 Jan 1478 (as written; Florentine style would make it 1479)
title: Anonymous cipher letter of 13 January 1478 in the Mazzinghi cipher (lead 2307), bare; MAP 72/170 glosses the same system
place: not stated (Rome likely, as for the sibling letters)
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza CXXXVII, doc. 252
folio_note: One oblong leaf, recto: head "+ adì 13 di gennaio 1478", about 20 lines of cipher with clear words between runs; verso blank. Inventory vol. 4 (filza CXXXVII, p. 281): "Lettera cifrata di anonimo ad anonimo. s. l., 1478 gen. 13, n. 252".
status: Bare: no interlinear or marginal decipherment (checked at 1272 px). why: A third letter of the January 1478 Medici series, three days before the Mazzinghi letter: more ciphertext for the same key, with the glossed 72/170 as the key source.
verify: Fold into the Mazzinghi lead (2307) or keep as a sibling; transcribe and apply the key rebuilt from 72/170.

title: "Magnifico Lorenzo" cipher letter with news from Naples; scattered letters over a few signs, otherwise bare
shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Firenze, Mediceo avanti il Principato, filza LXXII, doc. 216
folio_note: One leaf, recto and verso full (about 35 lines a side, heavy show-through): opens "Magnifico Lorenzo, a voi mi raccomando. Questo dì ... lettere da Napoli continenti come le cose ..." then cipher runs (letters, digits, Greek-like signs) between clear words. Not flagged in the inventory; found by the vetting session.
status: Mostly bare: a later hand wrote single letters or pairs (e, o, t, so, an ...) over some signs, a partial or attempted decipherment, not a running gloss. Those pairs are a start for the key.
why: A long Laurentian cipher letter about Naples, unread, with a few sign values already noted on the page.
verify: Transcribe both sides at full size; collect the superscript values; solve the rest (homophonic substitution).
